transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate you taking the time. Um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but my manager actually asked me to come in. It's probably just stress, you know how serving can get, but I've been getting a little mixed up on shift. 

I guess... well, I feel terrible because what scared everyone at work is that I started sort of freezing up in the middle of service. Just kind of stopping. Or doing things out of order? Like, I ended up just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out the checks. 

I didn't mean to freak anyone out, I think I was just overwhelmed. Does that make sense? I'm sure it's just from being overtired, right?
During that episode when you were standing by the soda station, do you remember what was happening at the time, or is that period blank/foggy when you try to recall it afterward?

Oh, um... no, it’s not blank at all. I actually remember it fine. I hope that’s a good thing? Like, I wasn't fainting or blacking out or anything scary like that, I promise. 

I knew I was standing there, I just... I don't know, my mind was just really full, I guess? Like I just got stuck for a minute and couldn't quite snap out of it to go back to my tables. But I remember being there and holding the key. It wasn't foggy, just... distracting. 

I'm really sorry if that sounds strange. I know I probably looked ridiculous to my coworkers. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

When you said your mind was 'really full' during that moment, can you tell me exactly what was going through your mind—were you overwhelmed by worries or thoughts, or did you notice anything unusual like hearing sounds or voices that others couldn't?

Oh, um... well, mostly I was just overwhelmed with all the tables. But... I guess, since you specifically asked... I really hope you don't think I'm crazy or anything. I'm sure it's just from being so exhausted, right? 

But sometimes, like during closing at the restaurant, or even when I'm just home in my own kitchen... I do hear this woman's voice. She'll just say my name, or she'll tell me I'm doing the drawer count wrong. It sounds so normal and clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize that nobody else is in the room, and nobody else heard it. 

I'm sure it's just my brain playing tricks on me from the stress. That happens to people when they work too much, doesn't it? I really try to just ignore it so I can keep doing a good job. I hope that's okay to share.
How long have you been hearing this woman's voice—did it start recently, around the same time as the freezing episodes, or has it been going on for a longer period, like weeks or months?

Oh, um... well, I really want to be helpful, so I'll just be completely honest with you. I hope that's okay. It hasn't just been the last few weeks. The voice... it's actually been getting a lot clearer for, gosh, maybe about four months now? 

And... well, I feel terrible even saying this out loud because I really do like my team, but for about four months I've also had this really firm feeling... or belief, I guess... that my coworkers and even some of the customers are targeting me. Like they're doing things on purpose to mess up my shifts. 

I know exactly how ridiculous that sounds, I really do, and I try so hard to just push it down so it doesn't affect my customer service! I don't want to cause any trouble at work. But yes, the clearer voices and feeling like everyone is targeting me, that's been happening for about four months. Does that make sense? I'm sure it's just a phase from being so burnt out, right?
Have you had any recent medical issues, head injuries, seizures, or new medications, or been using any drugs or alcohol, around the time these symptoms started?

Oh, um... no, nothing like that at all! I promise I'm really healthy otherwise. I haven't hit my head or had any seizures or anything scary. And I don't take any medications right now, except maybe some ibuprofen if I've been on my feet all day. 

And as for drugs or alcohol... oh gosh, no. I mean, I might have a glass of wine on my birthday or something, but I definitely don't do drugs or drink heavily. I know how important it is to be clear-headed for work, and I would never want to do anything to jeopardize my job. 

I'm really trying to take good care of myself, I swear. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure you know I'm not doing anything to cause this on purpose.

During these past four months, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood—like feeling very depressed, hopeless, or on the other end, unusually elevated, energetic, or euphoric for extended periods?

Oh, um... no, definitely not! I mean, I try really hard to stay positive, you know? I haven't felt depressed or hopeless or anything like that. I promise. Just... maybe a normal amount of tired from being on my feet at the restaurant, but nothing dark or sad. 

And I'm definitely not... unusually energetic or bouncing off the walls, either. Just my normal self. I always try to keep a good attitude and a big smile for the customers, so my mood has been pretty steady, I think. 

I hope that's helpful? I'm really trying to give you all the right information... I just don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. I'm doing okay emotionally, I really am. Is that what you were looking for?

Before these four months of hearing the voice and feeling targeted, did you notice any smaller changes—like being more withdrawn, having trouble concentrating, or feeling 'off' in yourself—going back even further, say five or six months ago?

Oh, um... well... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to give you the whole picture so you can help me—I did start feeling a little different before the last four months. I'm sorry I didn't mention it sooner! I just didn't want to sound like I was complaining about my job. 

But... yeah, this whole change in me, it's actually been building for a while. Gosh, maybe about a year and two months now? It started right around the time they asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. 

I was so honored they picked me, I really was! But I think maybe the pressure just made me a little more withdrawn, and I started feeling just... kind of 'off,' like you said. I really tried not to let it show at work, though. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this now? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you all the right details.

During that year when things started feeling 'off'—before the voice got clearer—did you notice yourself pulling away from friends or family, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or having a harder time keeping up with daily tasks?

Oh, um... well, I really try to keep up with everything, I promise. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, especially my husband. He works so hard. But... I guess, if I'm being perfectly honest... I haven't been doing as much of the things I used to love. 

I used to love going for walks on the beach, and baking, and tending to my little garden. And I'd write in my journal almost every day. But lately... I don't know, I just don't really do those things much anymore. It's not that I don't want to be a good wife or a fun person! It's just... I sit there when my husband tries to talk to me, and it's like I just can't get myself to care or start anything. 

I feel so terrible about it. I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or a bad partner. I'm trying my best to push through it, I swear. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer so you can help me get back to being myself again.

Over this past year or so, has the sense that people are targeting you, or hearing that woman's voice, been present continuously, or have there been stretches of weeks or months where those experiences went away completely?

Oh, um... well, I really want to give you the right answer here, but... I don't think I can say for sure if it ever went away completely. I mean, I try so hard to just ignore it and go to work and be normal, you know? 

I think... maybe there were days where I was just so busy at the restaurant that I didn't notice the voice as much, or maybe I just pushed the feeling of being targeted to the back of my mind because I had to focus on my tables. But as for like, whole weeks or months where it was just... gone? I don't... I don't think so. It's always kind of there, just under the surface, even when I'm trying my absolute hardest to be cheerful and pretend everything is fine. 

I'm sorry, I wish I could say it went away to make it sound less... crazy. I really hope I'm not making things too difficult for you by not having a clearer answer. Is it okay that it's been pretty much the whole time? I promise I've been trying to handle it as best as I can on my own.

Oh, um... well, I really want to give you the right answer here, but... I don't think I can say for sure if it ever went away completely. I mean, I try so hard to just ignore it and go to work and be normal, you know? 

I think... maybe there were days where I was just so busy at the restaurant that I didn't notice the voice as much, or maybe I just pushed the feeling of being targeted to the back of my mind because I had to focus on my tables. But as for like, whole weeks or months where it was just... gone? I don't... I don't think so. It's always kind of there, just under the surface, even when I'm trying my absolute hardest to be cheerful and pretend everything is fine. 

I'm sorry, I wish I could say it went away to make it sound less... crazy. I really hope I'm not making things too difficult for you by not having a clearer answer. Is it okay that it's been pretty much the whole time? I promise I've been trying to handle it as best as I can on my own.

inference.note: Continuous psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions) for over a year with prodromal negative symptoms (social withdrawal, anhedonia, avolition), no mood episode features, no substance/medical cause identified—consistent with schizophrenia rather than mood disorder with psychotic features or brief psychotic disorder.

opening_question.intent: Establish the primary reason for the visit today
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports over a year of persistent psychotic symptoms including auditory hallucinations (hearing a woman's voice commenting/commanding) and a fixed persecutory delusion (coworkers/customers targeting her), lasting continuously for ~4 months at full intensity with prodromal social withdrawal and anhedonia for ~14 months total. No mood episode (depressive or manic) accompanies the psychosis, ruling out schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder with psychotic features. No substance use, medical illness, or head injury accounts for symptoms. Functional impairment is evident (occupational dysfunction—freezing during shifts, errors, being sent in by manager) and social/marital withdrawal. Presentation meets criteria for Schizophrenia (Criterion A: hallucinations + delusions; Criterion B: functional decline; Criterion C: >6 months duration with prodromal and active phases).
